summary.text: Phara Souffrant Forrest is the Democratic and Working Families Party member of the Assembly for District 57 and won re-election on November 3, 2026.

A registered nurse and tenant organizer who is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, she defeated incumbent Walter Mosley in the 2020 Democratic primary, has been re-elected since, and won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.

paragraphs.text: Phara Souffrant Forrest was born in Brooklyn, according to Ballotpedia, and her official biography describes her as the daughter of Haitian immigrants and a lifelong resident of the 57th District who attended Brooklyn public schools, including Philippa Schuyler Middle School and Benjamin Banneker Academy for Community Development.

She attended SUNY Geneseo, where she majored in international relations (Ballotpedia lists a B.A. in 2011), then earned an associate degree in nursing from CUNY City Tech (2016) and a BSN from the CUNY School of Professional Studies.

Before her election, Souffrant Forrest worked in New York City public schools, as an Uber driver, and in youth advocacy at Global Kids, and then as a maternal child field nurse; she is a member of the New York State Nurses Association.
She was president of her building's tenant association (Ballotpedia names the 12 Crown Tenant Association) and is a member of the Crown Heights Tenant Union.
Her official biography says tenant organizing, including the push for the Housing Stability & Tenant Protection Act of 2019, motivated her to run for office.

Souffrant Forrest first won the seat by defeating incumbent Walter Mosley in the June 2020 Democratic primary and then winning the November 2020 general election, and she was re-elected in 2022 and 2024; Ballotpedia lists her tenure as beginning in 2021.

For the 2025-2026 session she is a member of the Aging, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Higher Education, Health, Insurance, and Social Services committees, and she chairs the Task Force on New Americans and its Subcommittee on Intergenerational Care.

Her official biography says she passed the Less Is More Act in her first term and has continued to focus on tenants' rights, healthcare access and carceral system reforms, and that she lives in Crown Heights with her husband and son.
On June 23, 2026 she won the Democratic primary over Samantha Johnson, 78.5% to 20.7%, and she is also on the Working Families Party line.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election over Yolanda Allison, according to unofficial results from the NYC Board of Elections.
